The combined scalar is then chained through computePotentialExchangeUpdate's dmu_lR_exchange_input_dpL via drho_LR_dpL (bulk sensitivity) only, even though the correctly-computed confined-density sensitivity drho_lR_exchange_input_dpL is threaded all the way into the function and available. Twenty-four questions accumulated across the 10 rounds and NOT ONE was answered or closed by the loop, by design - they are the items where a fix would have meant writing or changing a material parameter, an expected value, a tolerance literal, a BC magnitude or a sign convention (sections 1.1, 1.2, 3, 9), or where two rulebooks genuinely conflict and section 9 routes the call to him (q24, the uncalled computeMaxwellConjugateMicroPotential: ogs-ai says a function with no caller must not land, CLAUDE.md section 6.3 says a superseded definition is annotated historical and kept). text: AUTOSQUASH REHEARSAL (driver, session 2) - RESULT: NEGATIVE. It does NOT replay clean, and this supersedes session 1's HANDOFF claim that it did (that claim was true at dea92ed01c, before rounds 4-10 added eleven more fixups). Run in a THROWAWAY detached worktree off c268ac583d (never in the loop worktree - see the round-8 note on why). Command: GIT_EDITOR=true GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=true git rebase --autosquash --interactive c41ada5f75. FINDING 1: unattended autosquash STOPS ON CONFLICT. First stop is b1f170c9b9 (round 6's fixup) on Tests/ProcessLib/RichardsMechanics/StrainedFilmPotential.cpp, two hunks, both comment-only: round 4 had rewritten those comments to cite in-tree-looking deck paths, and round 6 then removed those same references as dangling (finding b50a5e88), so the two fixups edit the same lines. This is exactly the hazard round 7 recorded as q19; it is now CONFIRMED by execution, not just predicted. An instrumented replay hit FOUR conflict stops in total, the later ones including b7051af2ba (round 8's non-ASCII transliteration), which also rewrote comment lines earlier fixups had touched. FINDING 2, and the important one: a MECHANICAL conflict resolution is NOT safe here. Resolving each conflict by taking the final tip content for the whole conflicted file (`git checkout c268ac583d -- <file>`) does reach an empty tree diff against c268ac583d - verified, `git diff c268ac583d HEAD` empty - but it CORRUPTS THE COMMIT STRUCTURE: the result carries THREE commits instead of four, and the messages no longer match their contents (the commit holding the 68-file ProcessLib content ended up under the message 'Tests: unit tests for the double-structure micro-macro exchange'). So an empty tree diff is NOT sufficient evidence of a good squash - the commit/message pairing must be checked too. CONCLUSION AND HANDOFF: the squash needs per-hunk resolution by Vinay, because choosing which comment wording survives and which commit each hunk belongs to is an authorship call the loop does not own (CLAUDE.md §7, §9). It was deliberately NOT forced. The branch is therefore pushed WITH its fixups unsquashed, which is a valid MR-branch state; squashing stays a manual step. Caveat recorded honestly: part of the corruption in FINDING 2 is attributable to the blunt resolution strategy itself, not to the branch alone - the defensible claims are (a) unattended autosquash conflicts, four stops, and (b) whole-file resolution is unsafe.

APPROVED CODE CHANGES APPLIED 2026-09-22 (Vinay approved each explicitly; the loop's budget was already spent, so these are post-loop, not a round). Four fixup commits: aa78e267c6, 28913af8a6, 0a82f54e06, bc2dac021d. Tip c268ac583d -> bc2dac021d, 29 commits over c41ada5f75. (1) THE 21 CLANG-TIDY WarningsAsErrors HITS - the biggest thing found all day, and no review round found it because no round ran the tool. The project's own .clang-tidy lists readability-simplify-boolean-expr and readability-named-parameter in WarningsAsErrors, so these were `error:` not warnings, and would have blocked the MR at CI. 17 boolean-guard hits + 4 unnamed ioName parameters, all blaming to 569ba9dd15. KEY ENGINEERING CALL, made by the fixing agent and independently confirmed: De Morgan was NOT applied. clang-tidy's own fixit would rewrite `if (!(a && b))` to `if (!a || !b)`, which CHANGES NaN SEMANTICS - !(x > y) is true under NaN while (x <= y) is false. Five of the seventeen sites are genuinely NaN-reachable with no leading isfinite short-circuit (PotentialExchange.h:760 bisection bracket, :826 loaded/unloaded branch selector, CreateRichardsMechanicsProcess.cpp:795 PRJ input validation guarding an OGS_FATAL, RichardsMechanicsFEM-impl.h:674 macro-floor cutoff early-out, :1484 the 2x2 FD denominators). De Morgan there would have let a NaN through a bisection fallback, into the loaded branch, past a PRJ validity check, into the cutoff, and into a division. Instead every site was HOISTED: `bool const <name> = <predicate unchanged>; if (!<name>)`. Satisfies the check, preserves behaviour bit-for-bit. Explanatory comments added at the five NaN-critical sites. (2) q22 - two EXPECT_NEAR replaced by EXPECT_DOUBLE_EQ; this REMOVES the tolerance literals 1e-14 and 1e-12 rather than adding any, and both exact-zero contracts were re-verified in the producing functions first. (3) q16(a) - std::call_once WARN added at the two silent Newton exits, matching the two pre-existing loops in the same file; control flow and every number untouched, the policy half (reject the step / OGS_FATAL) remains Vinay's. (4) q14 - the four duplicate ctest registrations removed; beacon suite 13 -> 9 tests. VERIFICATION, three independent adversarial lanes: (a) EQUIVALENCE 17/17, zero defects, proven constructively by mechanically UN-HOISTING every declaration and token-diffing against base - PotentialExchange.h and CreateRichardsMechanicsProcess.cpp came back token-identical, so no swapped branch, dropped else or moved guard is possible; (b) SUITE - build clean with zero warnings, 46 tests / 44 passed / 2 pre-existing skips / 0 failed (exact baseline), beacon 9/9, all 39 RichardsMechanics-labelled ctests pass; (c) DRIFT AUDIT - zero code-side literal ADDITIONS anywhere; the only removals are the two q22 tolerances and four `RUNTIME 20` belonging to the deleted duplicate blocks; all comparison operators net to zero in the token census. NUMBER RECONCILIATION: the RichardsMechanics-label count is now 39, not the 43 recorded earlier today - the difference is exactly q14's four removed duplicates (43-4=39), not a lost test. POST-FIX GATE: re-running clang-tidy with the project config on CreateRichardsMechanicsProcess.cpp now reports 0 hits of the two CI-blocking checks, down from 5. No .prj file was touched by any of the four commits. ORCHESTRATOR ERROR, self-reported per CLAUDE.md §13.3(5) and §0.1. Vinay asked for the 8 citation REFUTATIONS to be audited, since a false kill is worse than a missed finding and two of the eight are the sole candidates for q5/q6. I built the per-refutation audit files by reading the workflow journal and pairing candidates[i] with verdicts[i]. THAT PAIRING WAS WRONG: the journal records each sub-agent's return in COMPLETION order, while the candidate list is in SUBMISSION order, and for parallel agents those differ. Every audit file therefore glued one candidate to a different verdict's reasoning. Consequence: the first audit pass (8 Opus auditors) reported 6 FALSE_KILLS, 1 KILL_RIGHT_WRONG_REASON and 1 UNRESOLVABLE, with a striking common finding that 'the body argues against a different candidate than the header'. THAT COMMON FINDING WAS THE SIGNATURE OF MY BUG, NOT A DEFECT IN THE REFUTATION PASS. The auditors were right to detect the mismatch and reasonable to attribute it to the refuters; they had no way to see the corruption was upstream of them. Detection: the uniformity of the 'mis-targeted' finding across six independent auditors was implausible for genuinely independent refuters, so I went back to the workflow's OWN returned citation_verdicts array - which carries the authoritative {candidate, verdict} pairing built inside the script - and found candidate 1 (q3+q4 porosity phi0) is STANDS there while my file filed it as refutation_01_REFUTED. Remediation: the corrupted files were ANNOTATED as historical rather than deleted (a `rm -rf` attempt was correctly blocked by the §6.2/§6.3 hook), a correctly-paired set was rebuilt from the authoritative array into scratchpad/refutations_correct/, and the audit was re-run from scratch with the auditors explicitly told about the invalidated attempt and instructed to carry nothing over from it. NOTHING FROM THE FIRST AUDIT PASS SHOULD BE RELIED ON. Standing lesson: when reconstructing pairs from a parallel workflow's journal, pair by the agent's own recorded input or by the script's returned pairing - never by row order, which is completion order.

AUDIT OF THE EIGHT REFUTATIONS (Vinay asked for this; CLAUDE.md §13.3(5)). Run on CORRECTLY-paired files after my pairing bug was found and recorded; local sources only, per Vinay's instruction not to reach the MacBook over a fragile link. FIRM, where the individual auditor and the independent synthesis AGREE and I verified the arithmetic myself: (1) E route A is a FALSE KILL. The refutation's decisive sentence was that 'the source's own prescription yields 36 MPa', obtained as E_min = 3*20*(1-2*0.20) = 36 using the DECK's nu=0.2 inside the SOURCE's formula. BEACON D3.3 p.212 defines E_min as the Young modulus corresponding to the minimum bulk modulus via Eq.(18) E = 3K(1-2nu), and the only nu in LEI's Test1a01 set is the 0.35 in the same Table 4-1, giving E_min = 18.0 MPa. D3.3 states no numeric E_min anywhere (full-text census). So at the table's own e0 = 0.68, E = max(13/0.68^2, 18.0) = max(28.11, 18.0) = 28.11 MPa and THE FLOOR DOES NOT BIND; it engages only above e = sqrt(13/18) = 0.850. I read Table 4-1 from the 200 dpi page IMAGE myself because text extraction destroys the e^2 exponent, and recomputed both numbers independently. (2) The nu candidates are FALSE KILLS and cost nothing: all five beacon decks already carry nu = 0.2, and D3.3 p.66 Table 2 (BGR Annex A, authors Kumar and Beese) states 0.2, so adopting it DOCUMENTS the existing literal rather than changing it. (3) Candidate 01, porosity phi0 = 0.4 from D3.3 p.214 Table 4-1, STANDS and matches the 1a01 decks exactly - also a pure documentation win. THE SYSTEMATIC DEFECT, and it is mine: my refutation prompt told the refuters to 'default to REFUTED when uncertain'. That biased them into conflating 'adopting this would change a deck literal' with 'the citation is invalid'. Those are different findings - a source giving a different value is a valid candidate whose adoption is Vinay's §1.1 call, not grounds for a kill. Several kills turn on exactly that conflation.
